Subject: Security gate definitions & escalation path — FinSecure evaluation

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our discussion I pulled together a concise security gate definition that we can embed into the Mutual Action Plan so your procurement and security teams have deterministic acceptance criteria. High level notes below — I attached a one-page MAP + an evidence index.

Security gates we propose for the evaluation (ordered by when they typically unblock a pilot):
- SOC 2 Type II: provide latest SOC 2 report (or SOC bridge) plus a commitment to annual attestations; acceptance = reviewer confirms no high-severity exceptions impacting data handling.
- SIG/CAIQ: completed questionnaire + evidence index for answers marked "partial" or "not applicable"; acceptance = SIG scorecard shared and follow-up items scheduled.
- DPA & Security Addendum: DPA draft in review; we support both vendor-provided and in-line redlines; acceptance = executed DPA or DocuSign envelope signed.
- Data retention & logs: default production retention for request logs: 30 days; audit logs: 365 days; backups: encrypted and retained for 365 days unless otherwise specified in DPA; acceptance = retention table confirmed and added to DPA.
- Key management: support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) on Dedicated/Private + encryption at rest for Hosted; acceptance = KMS integration plan or attestation.

Escalation path (if a gate blocks close):
1) Technical clarifying question -> assigned engineer (cc'd Sean).
2) Security clarification or control gap -> Naomi (Security & Compliance).
3) Contract or DPA impasse -> Laura (Legal) + Sales leadership.

Proposed timeline to close the MAP:
- Week 0 (this week): Share SIG/CAIQ draft + initial evidence index (attached).
- Week 1: FinSecure reviews SOC 2 and SIG answers; rounds of Q&A.
- Week 2: DPA redlines exchanged; retention and KMS finalized.
- Week 3: Final sign-off and DocuSign.

Can you confirm these gates look complete from FinSecure's side and whether the retention windows above are acceptable as a starting point? If there's a hard internal requirement (e.g., 7-year retention or specific backup rules) call that out and we'll surface with the product team.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0118

Attachments: MAP_v1.3.pdf (MAP + acceptance criteria), security-evidence-index.xlsx (evidence pointers)

From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@finsecure.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@finsecure.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security gate definitions & escalation path — FinSecure evaluation

Marcus — thanks for the crisp summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) SOC 2: we require the latest Type II for the same 12-month period our pilot will span; if Redwood only has Type I or a bridge letter we need the SOC 2 scope and remediation plan in writing.
2) Data retention: our default requirement for audit logs is 3 years, not 1; do you support configurable retention beyond 365 days in Dedicated/Private? Also need clarity on deletion policy for PII on request.
3) KMS: BYOK is preferred for production but for the pilot we can accept provider-managed keys if encryption at rest is demonstrated and access controls audited.
4) SIG/CAIQ: we'll assign our security analyst to go through the CAIQ; please confirm which attachments in the evidence index map to each CAIQ question.

I'll loop in our Legal Ops (cc'd) for DPA redlines. We can commit to the Week 0–3 cadence if the retention & SOC 2 items are addressed in Week 1.

Best,
Alex Novak
Head of Platform Security | FinSecure
alex.novak@finsecure.com

Marcus / Sean — quick internal note on next steps after Alex's ask: 

- SOC 2: I'll check with Compliance to confirm whether we can provide the 12-month Type II aligned to FinSecure's pilot dates. If not, we'll prepare a bridge letter + remediation timeline.
- Retention: product supports per-tenant retention on Dedicated/Private today; Hosted currently supports up to 365 days for audit logs but we can propose a retention extension via Dedicated or a custom SLA. We should flag the 3-year ask as a product/infrastructure change for Legal to evaluate.
- PII deletion: we'll prepare a one-page process doc describing deletion flows, scope, and timelines (subject to DPA language).

I recommend we present two tracks to FinSecure in Week 1: (A) Pilot on Hosted with provider keys + documentation (fastest), (B) Pilot on Dedicated with BYOK + 3-year retention (longer but meets their ask). That gives them a clear choice and helps unblock timelines.

I'll gather the evidence attachments and annotate the CAIQ mapping in the attached spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow. Sean — please be ready to run through the KMS and retention demo if they pick Option B.

Alex / Legal Ops — looping in from Redwood Legal. We reviewed Marcus' proposed gates and Naomi's two-track approach and have a couple of pragmatic asks before we exchange redlines: 

1) Please confirm whether FinSecure will accept an executed DPA limited to the pilot scope (timeboxed) with a follow-on enterprise DPA to be negotiated on expansion. That usually accelerates sign-off.
2) On retention: if you require 3 years for audit logs, please provide the specific regulation or internal policy doc so we can map obligations to product capabilities. We can add a custom clause to the pilot DPA if needed.

We'll prepare a first-pass DPA with pilot-limited retention options and an explicit escalation clause to handle permanent changes post-pilot. Link to the draft will be shared via DocuSign so we can track approvals.
